max_tire.note: Owners on aftermarket 20s report no rubbing, and 275/70R18 fits on Toyota TRD 18s. 285/50R22 on the factory 22s needed cutting and spacers.

items.title: V35A engine main-bearing debris
items.summary: Machining debris can cause main-bearing failure and a stall. Dealers replace the engine.

items.title: V35A engine main-bearing debris (expansion)
items.summary: Expands 24V-381. Dealers inspect the #1 main bearing and replace the engine if needed (Lexus 25LA07).

items.title: Unexpected movement in neutral
items.summary: The vehicle may move in neutral with the brakes off. Dealers update the transmission ECU software.

items.title: Passenger seat occupant-classification sensor
items.summary: Too little clearance at the seat frame stopper can confuse the OCS sensor. Dealers inspect and replace the seat frame as needed.

items.title: Transmission/engine ECU communication
items.summary: If a transmission solenoid fails, the ECUs may stop communicating and the transmission can be damaged. Dealers update the transmission ECU software.

items.title: Panoramic View Monitor camera freeze
items.summary: The rear camera image may freeze or go blank in reverse. Dealers update the software.

items.title: VSC may not re-enable on restart
items.summary: Skid Control ECU software may leave VSC off after a restart. Dealers update the software.

timeline.change: Revealed October 13, 2021 on the GA-F platform: V35A 3.4 twin-turbo V6 (409 hp, 479 lb-ft), 10-speed automatic, 441 lb lighter than the LX 570. Standard, Premium, Luxury, F Sport and four-seat Ultra Luxury grades.
Engine recalls 24V-381 and 25V-767 cover main-bearing debris. Owners also report a clunk into first on rolling stops.
Lexus Safety System+ 2.5 standard. The F Sport Handling has 22-in forged wheels and a Torsen limited-slip rear differential.
LX 700h hybrid joins the range, including the Overtrail with front and rear lockers plus the center lock (revealed October 10, 2024).
Minor updates: darker 20-in wheels and a digital mirror on Premium, red calipers and Palomino leather on F Sport Handling, and power-folding rear seats on F Sport Handling and Overtrail.

identify.intro: Every US LX 600 is built at the same plant on the same platform as the Land Cruiser 300, so the real differences are grade, AHC and recall status.

items.head: VIN
items.body: US trucks start JTJ and carry 7CX in positions 6–8. NHTSA's vPIC decoder reads them as the 310 Series with the V35A-FTS, built at Toyota Auto Body's Yoshiwara plant. The 10th character is the model year (N = 2022, P = 2023, R = 2024, S = 2025).

items.head: Lockers
items.body: US LX 600s have a lockable center diff only. Triple locks came on Japan's LX Offroad grade and, in the US, on the LX 700h Overtrail, which is a different model.

items.head: F Sport Handling
items.body: 22-in forged wheels and a Torsen limited-slip rear differential.

items.head: AHC or not
items.body: Most trucks have Active Height Control, but Slee Off-Road's build was a Premium custom-ordered without AHC so it could run Dobinsons suspension. Check before planning a lift.

items.head: Engine recall status
items.body: 2022–2024 trucks may be in 24V-381 or 25V-767 (Lexus 25LA07). Ask for paperwork showing the inspection or replacement engine.

values.intro: A current model, so the new-car window sticker sets the market. Used trucks are only just starting to show up at auction.
values.note: MSRPs include the $1,550 destination fee. On Bring a Trailer, a 2024 LX 600 Premium sold for $87,500 in April 2026, and a 2023 Ultra Luxury was bid to $104,000 without selling.
